gap: No result ChatGPT got compares how long each of the lightest 1 kWh LiFePO4 stations takes to refill from the car's own 12 V socket while driving. The Explorer 1000 v2 takes about 11–12 h (12 V × 8 A), the C1000 Gen 2 about 10.4 h through its XT60 input (12 V × 8.2 A), and BLUETTI's 'full in 1.8 hours' on-the-go claim for the Elite 100 V2 depends on the separate Charger 1 accessory.
standout_why: I opened backup-power.org (cited), solarpowerauditor.com/camping (cited), juicebench.com and our own current page. backup-power.org lists the 12 V car port only as an output and gives no car-charging input or hours. juicebench gives AC charge minutes and Wh/kg but nothing for car charging. solarpowerauditor already covers usable Wh per lb, fridge hours and 2×100 W solar refill time (Explorer 1000 v2: 905 Wh usable, 38.0 Wh/lb, 7 h 08 min), but has no car-socket figure. Our page has no car-input column. One overlap: Jackery's own FAQ (faq.jackery.com, a result in two chats) states 'Around 12H' for the Explorer 1000 v2. So the Jackery number alone is not new. The side-by-side comparison and the BLUETTI accessory caveat are new.
decides: This confirms the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 as the pick rather than changing it. Car-socket refill takes about 10–12 h on every candidate I could source, so the lightest unit gives nothing up on the drive. The finding also takes away a reason to switch to the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2: its 1.8 h on-the-road figure needs the Charger 1 accessory, which OutdoorGearLab calls a $250 inverter charger that must be installed in the car. Through the dashboard socket it is no faster.

findings.label: Car-socket input (maker)
findings.note: Jackery gives no wattage. At 12 V: 12 V × 8 A = 96 W.

findings.label: Hours to refill from a 12 V car socket
findings.note: 1,070 Wh ÷ 96 W = 11.1 h before losses. The maker's 'Around 12H' implies about 89 W delivered.

findings.label: Solar refill hours with Jackery's own panels (maker)
findings.value: 2× SolarSaga 100: ≈8 h; 2× SolarSaga 200: ≈3.8 h; 1× SolarSaga 100: ≈15 h
findings.note: Times as Jackery states them. The solar input is 200 W per port and 400 W across both ports, 16–60 V.

findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 – Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Anker's page has no car-socket charge time. CleanTechnica (https://cleantechnica.com/2025/09/24/the-anker-solix-c1000-gen-2-portable-power-station-cleantechnica-tested/, read 2026-11-14) mentions a 12-volt automotive adapter that ends in an XT60 plug, but gives no rate.

findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 – Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: 12 V × 8.2 A = 98.4 W; 1,024 Wh ÷ 98.4 W = 10.4 h before losses. Assumes the socket supplies the full 8.2 A.

findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 – Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: 1,024 ÷ 24.9 = 41.1 Wh/lb. The page showed no price when I read it.

findings.label: On-the-go charge claim and what it needs (maker)
findings.value: 'On-the-Go Charging – Full in 1.8 Hours' via BLUETTI Charger 1; solar/DC input 1,000 W max, 12–60 V, 20 A max
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station – BLUETTI US
findings.note: The page says 'Recharge via BLUETTI Charger 1 while driving' and gives no plain 12 V socket figure. 1,024 Wh ÷ 1.8 h = 569 W, which matches the 560 W Charger 1 rate, not a dashboard socket.

findings.label: What the fast car charging requires (named reviewer)
findings.value: OutdoorGearLab: the '6x faster' car charging needs a '$250 inverter charger that requires installation in your car'
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab gives no measured time for plain 12 V socket charging.

findings.label: Usable Wh per lb, measured (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab measured 890 Wh usable (87%) and 25.0 lb on its scale: 890 ÷ 25.0 = 35.6 Wh/lb. For comparison, solarpowerauditor lists 905 Wh usable for the Explorer 1000 v2: 905 ÷ 23.8 = 38.0.

findings.label: Price (maker US store)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station – BLUETTI US
findings.note: This is the standard Elite 100 V2. The Bio-based version is listed at US$699.00. $499 ÷ 1,024 Wh = $0.49/Wh.

findings.label: Alternator-charger refill time (named reviewer)
findings.value: 1.3 h with the optional 800 W alternator charger
findings.note: This is an accessory route, not the 12 V socket: 1,024 Wh ÷ 800 W = 1.28 h. StorageReview lists 27.6 lb.
